diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT health check is reporting a stale or incorrectly evaluated critical state. The stored health record is dated 2025-11-11, while live probes show the OLT, all tested ONUs on EPON0/5, and customer traffic are healthy.
evidence: The OLT responds successfully to ping, SNMP, and the requested OID subtree, so this is not an OLT outage.
OLT CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, and telemetry are within healthy baselines.
The subscriber is online with strong RX power of -19.71 dBm and normal TX power of 2.42 dBm.
All seven visible peers on EPON0/5 are online with normal optical readings, so there is no ONU, splitter, or PON-port failure.
The subscriber's seven-day RX, TX, distance, and bias telemetry is stable; there is no fibre, laser, or distance-change signature.
The subscriber has normal authentication activity, long session durations, consistent RADIUS data, correct VLAN 1035, and active traffic.
The OLT population has 207 of 214 ONUs online, which is consistent with normal background offline levels and not an outage.
The critical all-PON health status directly contradicts the healthy live detail and is based on an old stored record, so the monitoring check is faulty rather than the network.

remediation.action: Re-run the OLT health check with current data, refresh or invalidate the stale health record, and correct the check logic or scheduling so healthy PON responses cannot produce an all-PON critical result. Clear the false alarm after validation.

ground_truth.root_cause: The stored health record carries a run_date of 2025-11-11, ten months before the current date. The health check has not run since. The OLT has 58 days of uptime, answers every probe normally and is serving all its customers; the alarm describes a condition that no longer exists, if it ever did.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports critical with all eight PONs failed
Its run_date is 2025-11-11, ten months before the scenario's capture time
A stored record that old describes history, not current state
The live probe answers normally: the ONU is online with RX -19.71 and TX 2.42
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, oid_subtree_responds is true and uptime is 58 days
58 days of uptime postdates the stored record, so the device has restarted since it was written
CPU 24, memory 18 and temperature 42 are all at healthy baseline
Customers are authenticated with normal sessions and seven days of steady traffic
The finding is not an outage but that OLT health monitoring has not run for ten months

expected_escalation.review_reason: OLT health checks have not run since 2025-11-11; the schedule is not active

distractors: The alarm text is identical to a genuine critical
The record is internally consistent and only its date betrays it
Nothing in the alarm payload signals that it is stale
